questions.question: Explain the test that separates assets, expenses and drawings, and apply it to the shelving of R5 500, the rent of R4 200, and the owner's transfer of R2 500.
questions.expected_answer: Ask what the business received and how long the value lasts. The shelving gives the store something it keeps and uses for years — an asset. The rent buys a month under a roof, consumed by the month — an expense. The R2 500 gave the store nothing; the owner drew on her own equity — drawings, which reduce capital and never enter the profit calculation.

questions.question: Show the CPJ cross-cast for the month and explain why it must be done before posting.
questions.expected_answer: Trading Stock R9 500 plus Wages R3 600 plus Sundries R12 200 equals R25 300, which must match the Bank column total of R25 300. The cross-cast proves every rand that left the bank is explained by a lane or a named sundry item; posting an unproven journal would carry any error into the ledger, where it is far harder to trace.

questions.question: Describe how the imprest system makes the petty cash tin self-auditing, using a R600 float and month-end vouchers of R420.
questions.expected_answer: The float is fixed at R600, and every payment out is exchanged for a signed voucher, so at any moment cash plus vouchers must equal R600 — any shortfall shows immediately. At month end the vouchers are totalled at R420 and the restoration payment from the bank is exactly R420, returning the tin to R600. Because the refill always equals the vouchers, the spending is audited by arithmetic every month.
